src/business/services/SchedulingService.ts: the mapping `new Appointment(a.id, a.patientId, a.practitionerId, a.startsAt, a.minutes, a.status as AppointmentStatus)` appears in both book() and cancel()
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module's concern is cohesive: both services handle the appointment workflow, booking and cancelling visits and writing notes on them. The abstraction and boundary are not consistent, though. SchedulingService uses persistence DAOs (PatientDao, AppointmentDao) and maps their rows into domain entities (Appointment, Patient, Practitioner). VisitNotesService uses Prisma directly and has no domain entity. Worse, VisitNotesService bypasses its own injected abstraction: write() uses the injected PrismaService, while notesFor() creates a separate `new PrismaClient()`. That means the same class gets data through two different routes. SchedulingService also repeats the mapping from a persistence row to an Appointment entity in two places, so that rule does not live in one place.

violations.message: notesFor() creates `new PrismaClient()` and skips the injected PrismaService that write() uses, so data access runs through two different paths in one class.
This service uses Prisma directly and returns plain VisitNote objects. That doesn't match the module's DAO-plus-entity pattern used in SchedulingService.
The mapping from a persistence row to an Appointment entity is repeated inline in book() and cancel() instead of living in one place.
